title: Max Consecutive Ones III
description: Brute force to optimized: re-walking from every start versus a single coordinated variable-size sliding window tracking a zero-count budget.

blocks.text: Given a binary array nums and an integer k, you may flip at most k zeros to ones. Return the maximum number of consecutive ones (1s) achievable after doing so.

blocks.caption: Grow the window, spending up to k flips on zeros inside it

blocks.text: Given a binary array nums and an integer k, find the length of the longest contiguous stretch that could be made entirely 1s by flipping at most k of its zeros.

blocks.title: Analogy: Flip Tokens for Zeros
blocks.text: Like being handed k flip tokens, and walking through a row of coin flips (0 = tails, 1 = heads), spending one token to mentally treat a tails as heads. The longest stretch walkable before running out of tokens, without ever unspending one, is the answer.

blocks.caption: Spend a flip token on every zero entering the window, refund one when a zero leaves

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Result","Why"],"rows":[["The window at indices 4-9: [0,0,1,1,1,1]","Contains exactly 2 zeros (indices 4 and 5)","Flipping both zeros makes all 6 positions 1s, matching the flip budget of k=2"],["Answer","6","This is the longest stretch containing at most 2 zeros"]]}

{"headers":["Step","Result","Why"],"rows":[["The window at indices 2-11: [1,1,0,0,1,1,1,0,1,1]","Contains exactly 3 zeros (indices 4, 5, and 9)","Flipping all 3 zeros makes all 10 positions 1s, matching the flip budget of k=3"],["Answer","10","This is the longest stretch containing at most 3 zeros"]]}

blocks.text: When no flips are allowed at all, the answer is simply the length of the longest existing run of 1s, since the zero-count budget of the window can never exceed 0.
Before physically trying every possible flip combination, notice that flipping a zero doesn't need to actually happen. Tracking how many zeros currently sit inside a candidate window is enough.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: "Flip at most k zeros" is equivalent to "tolerate at most k zeros in the window without flipping them at all", since the flipped window's length is identical either way.

Observation 2: This turns the problem into finding the longest window containing at most k zeros, the exact same shape as Longest Repeating Character Replacement's "at most k replacements" and Fruit Into Baskets's "at most k distinct types".

Observation 3: Grow a window from the right, incrementing a zero counter whenever a zero enters. Whenever that counter exceeds k, shrink from the left (decrementing the counter whenever a zero leaves) until it's back to at most k.

Observation 4: Track the maximum window length seen throughout this single coordinated pass.

Recognizing "at most k of a certain kind of element" as a reusable variable-size sliding window shape immediately suggests tracking a single running counter, rather than simulating actual flips.
This is a direct instance of the "at most k tolerance" variable-size sliding window pattern, with zeros as the tolerated element.
For every possible starting index, walk forward, counting zeros, stopping the moment the zero count would exceed k.

items: For every possible starting index, walk forward one element at a time, counting zeros encountered so far.
Stop extending the moment the zero count would exceed k, and record the length of the stretch collected so far.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: A fresh zero counter is used for every starting position, since each independent walk needs to track its own zero budget.
The inner walk breaks immediately once the zero count exceeds k, since continuing further from this same start could never help.
best only ever increases, tracking the single longest qualifying stretch found across every starting position.

blocks.text: Every possible starting position is checked directly, walking forward until the zero budget is exceeded, so the correct maximum is always found.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n squared) in the worst case, since each of the n starting positions can walk forward up to n elements.
Space: O(1) extra.

Limitation: restarting the zero count from scratch at every new starting position ignores that a single coordinated sliding window, sharing the same running zero counter, can answer the same question in one linear pass.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: The brute force treats every starting index independently, discarding useful information between them. Instead, grow a single window from the right, incrementing a zero counter whenever a zero enters. Whenever the counter exceeds k, shrink from the left, decrementing the counter whenever a zero leaves, until it's back within budget. Since the left pointer only ever moves forward and never resets, the entire process runs in a single linear pass.

Maintain a window with a left and right boundary, along with a running count of zeros in the window. Grow the window by advancing right. Whenever the zero count exceeds k, shrink from the left until it's at most k again. Track the maximum window length seen throughout.
Grow the window from the right, shrinking from the left only when the zero count exceeds k.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n), since left and right each advance forward at most n times total across the whole pass.
Space: O(1) extra.

The zero counter tracks exactly how many zeros currently fall within the window. It exceeding k means more flips would be needed than allowed, and shrinking from the left (decrementing the counter whenever the removed element is a zero) restores the window to a valid, at-most-k-zeros state.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","What happens"],"rows":[["Window has at most k zeros","Keep growing the window by advancing right"],["Window has more than k zeros","Shrink from the left until the zero count is at most k again"]]}

items: The zero counter is updated every time an element enters the window (on growth) or leaves it (on shrink), always reflecting the window's current zero total.
The shrink is a while loop, since more than one element might need to be removed from the left before the zero count drops back to at most k.
best is updated after any needed shrinking, always reflecting a currently-valid window's true length.

items: Trying to actually simulate or track which specific zeros get flipped, when only a running zero count is ever needed.
Shrinking the window by only one position instead of using a while loop, which can leave the zero count still over budget if multiple zeros needed removing.
Forgetting that best should be measured after any needed shrinking, on the now-valid window.

items: State explicitly that "flip at most k zeros" is equivalent to "tolerate at most k zeros without flipping", since this reframing is the key insight that unlocks the sliding window.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: "Flip/change/replace at most k elements to maximize a contiguous run" points toward a variable-size sliding window tracking a single running counter of the tolerated element, shrinking whenever that counter exceeds k.

items: How would you also report the actual indices to flip, not just the length? Track the window bounds (left, right) at the moment best is updated, and scan that window for its zero positions afterward.

How does this compare to Longest Repeating Character Replacement? Both track "at most k of a tolerated condition" in a variable-size window; this problem's tolerated condition (being a zero) is fixed, while that problem's condition (not matching the most frequent letter) changes as the window's contents change.
What if flips could also turn a 1 into a 0? That reframes the problem entirely, since it would no longer be a single-direction "tolerate up to k of one value" question.

A direct instance of the "at most k tolerance" technique shared with Longest Repeating Character Replacement and Fruit Into Baskets, just with a fixed tolerated value (zero) instead of a frequency-based one.
Shares its variable-size sliding window shape with Minimum Size Subarray Sum, just with a different growth/shrink condition.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text:
Brute force: O(n squared) time, O(1) space.
Optimized (variable-size sliding window): O(n) time, O(1) space.

items: Pattern: Variable-size sliding window with a running zero counter, the "at most k tolerance" pattern
Core Idea: Grow the window until the zero count exceeds k, then shrink from the left until it's back within budget
Time: O(n)
Space: O(1)
Most Important Observation: Flipping a zero never needs to actually happen, only counting how many zeros currently sit in the window
Interview Difficulty: Medium
One-line memory trick: Track zeros in the window, shrink when zeros exceed k
